svg.title: Layered Logic Mirror — First-boot Setup (SoftAP captive) screen wireframe
svg.desc: Lo-fi wireframe of the first-time-user Wi-Fi provisioning screen in the Layered Logic Mirror app. Shows the resting state (connection-to-mirror status pill, "Mirror needs Wi-Fi setup" prompt with skip-this-step option, SSID + password inputs with show/hide, WPA2 length validation, primary "Connect to Wi-Fi" submit button) with 6 numbered callouts pairing each design decision to its source rationale. A 4-thumbnail strip below documents the initial empty, password-shown, submitting/countdown, and timeout-recovery alternate states. A separate "Deferred — BLE provisioning" section at the bottom documents the post-V1 path with a dashed-border placeholder mockup of in-app success confirmation, the key advantage BLE has over SoftAP (where teardown kills the WS link before success/failure can be reported). Phone proportions match Pixel 9 (360x800 dp, 9:20 ratio). Brand indigo (#3214FF) marks the primary affordances.
svg.text: Layered Logic Mirror · App/v1 · Mobile (React Native, Pixel 9)
You're connected to the mirror's SoftAP. Give it
credentials for your home Wi-Fi to join, or tap
below to skip and control it directly over the SoftAP.
V1 ships SoftAP-only — works without an app (any browser at
192.168.4.1 reaches the captive webapp). BLE provisioning would
avoid the SoftAP-teardown error problem (see ④) but adds Bluetooth
scan-permission UX + a parallel pairing flow. Deferred to post-V1.
Skip path → works out of the box
"Control directly" bypasses Wi-Fi setup entirely — user keeps
their phone on the mirror's SoftAP and controls it from there.
Aligns with the locked product principle: works out of the box
with no required smart-home connection. Home Wi-Fi is opt-in.
WPA2 passwords are usually 12-30 chars of mixed entropy; typos
are the dominant failure mode for first-cred submission. Show
button is per-field (only password, not SSID), and reverts to
Hide after a successful submit so re-attempts start safe.
Static helper line below the password field; flips to an inline
error ("WPA2 passwords are at least 8 characters") when length
is 1-7. Catches the most common pre-submit error without sending
a fail to the firmware (where the SoftAP teardown amplifies it).
Status pill anchors the mental model
"Connected to mirror via SoftAP" tells the user they're talking
to the device, not their home network — critical because the next
step (submit) tears that connection down. Setting expectation
here reduces the "did something break?" reaction to the disconnect.
Verb describes what the device will do (attempt to join), not
what the form will do (persist creds). On submit, button text
switches to "Connecting…" — confirms the gesture landed and
disables to prevent double-submit during the 15s window.
Pre-input, password-visible, in-flight, and post-failure states the resting wireframe doesn't show.

verify before submit — typos in long
WPA2 passwords are the #1 fail mode.

Not built in V1. Documented here so the design rationale captures the path we'd take rather than pretending it doesn't exist.
BLE provisioning fixes the bug #6 root cause: the comm channel doesn't depend on Wi-Fi state, so the device CAN report success
or failure of the join attempt back to the app in real time.
No SoftAP teardown blind-spot — the BLE link
survives the cred-test and surfaces the real reason
Trigger to build: real user friction
from the bare-bones SoftAP error flow.
